name: Linezolid
route_note: Oral tablets or suspension, or IV infusion, twice daily; near-complete oral bioavailability allows early switch.
targets: 23S rRNA of the 50S ribosomal subunit (peptidyl transferase centre)

discovery.note: Developed in the 1990s from earlier DuPont oxazolidinones; the first marketed member of a new antibiotic class in decades. Year of the first published description (U-100766; Brickner et al., J Med Chem 1996).

tagline: First oxazolidinone: oral option for MRSA, VRE and drug-resistant tuberculosis
summary: Linezolid is a fully synthetic oxazolidinone antibiotic approved in 2000, active against MRSA, vancomycin-resistant enterococci and penicillin-resistant pneumococci. It is also a core component of modern regimens for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis, limited by bone-marrow and nerve toxicity with prolonged use.
mechanism: Linezolid binds the A-site pocket of the peptidyl transferase centre on 23S rRNA in the 50S ribosomal subunit, preventing correct positioning of aminoacyl-tRNA and blocking formation of the 70S initiation complex; protein synthesis is inhibited.

It is generally bacteriostatic against staphylococci and enterococci and bactericidal against most streptococci. Resistance arises through 23S rRNA mutations (e.g. G2576T) or the transferable cfr methyltransferase. It is also a weak reversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase.
uses: Nosocomial and community-acquired pneumonia caused by Gram-positive bacteria including MRSA

history.title: US approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Zyvox, the first oxazolidinone.

history.title: First resistance
history.detail: Linezolid-resistant S. aureus is reported shortly after approval.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic linezolid becomes available in the US after patent expiry.

history.title: WHO AWaRe classification
history.detail: WHO begins grouping antibiotics on its Essential Medicines List into Access, Watch and Reserve; linezolid is a Reserve antibiotic.

history.title: BPaL regimen
history.detail: The FDA approves pretomanid for use with bedaquiline and linezolid for highly drug-resistant TB.

history.title: WHO BPaLM
history.detail: WHO recommends six-month BPaLM (bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, moxifloxacin) for rifampicin-resistant TB.

pk.metabolism: non-enzymatic oxidation of the morpholine ring

serious: Peripheral and optic neuropathy with prolonged use

facts: Linezolid was the first new structural class of antibacterial approved in the US in about 35 years.

references.title: J Med Chem: Brickner et al. 1996, Synthesis and antibacterial activity of U-100592 and U-100766
